lines.trans: Fedya, tell me, did you by any chance study in France?
I have nothing better to do than to study there!
You have simply stunning fish searing technique.
I simply fry fish on a hot pan.
Such searing is only done in Lyon at Bocuse's.
Are you seriously comparing me with a French master?
Absolutely seriously, you have a rare natural gift.
No one has ever spoken such words to me before.
Real talent is always visible at first sight.
Thank you very much for such a high praise, chef.
Keep cooking, the guests will be in complete delight.
I promise to make the most delicious dish today!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да это не воровство, послушай! Это абсолютно безопасно.
examples.trans: That's not stealing, listen! It's completely safe.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'гляд'). Common masculine noun meaning 'look, glance' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('view, opinion') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Really? Did you notice his looks?

examples.text: Настоящий талант всегда виден с первого взгляда.
examples.trans: Real talent is always visible at first sight.

meanings.note: able to be seen; short form: виден, видна, видно

examples.text: Настоящий талант всегда виден с первого взгляда.
examples.trans: Real talent is always visible at first sight.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'delight', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Все гости были в полном восторге от ужина.
examples.trans: All the guests were completely delighted with the dinner.

examples.text: Мои гости будут в полном восторге!
examples.trans: My guests will be in total delight!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'high', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'gift', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Абсолютно серьёзно, у вас редкий природный дар.
examples.trans: Absolutely seriously, you have a rare natural gift.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to fry', forming an aspectual pair with 'пожарить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Повар жарит сочное мясо на сковороде.
examples.trans: The cook fries juicy meat on the pan.

examples.text: Нет, Федя сам жарил эту куропатку!
examples.trans: No, Fedya roasted that partridge himself!

examples.text: Я просто жарю рыбу на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: I simply fry fish on a hot pan.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'technician', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Они совсем не похожи на настоящих мастеров.
examples.trans: They look nothing like real technicians.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ dative + infinitive: мне терять нечего = I have nothing to lose

examples.trans: There is nothing to do here.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, что я хочу. Мне терять нечего.
examples.trans: You know what I want. I have nothing to lose.

meanings.note: used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: culinary technique of frying or roasting

examples.text: У вас просто потрясающая техника обжарки рыбы.
examples.trans: You have simply stunning fish searing technique.

examples.text: Такую обжарку делают только в Лионе у Бокюза.
examples.trans: Such searing is only done in Lyon at Bocuse's.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'evaluation'.

examples.trans: The critic gave a high rating to the restaurant.

examples.text: Погоди, нам нужна более объективная оценка.
examples.trans: Wait, we need a more objective opinion.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'first', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'full' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('complete, total, utter') (полный кошмар = a total nightmare) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'трясающий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('amazing, stunning').
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'natural' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Абсолютно серьёзно, у вас редкий природный дар.
examples.trans: Absolutely seriously, you have a rare natural gift.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'earlier'.

examples.text: В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Uncle Misha used to live in my room.
There used to be an old park here.

examples.text: Подождите. В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Wait. Uncle Misha used to live in my room.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'rare', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: У меня есть много редких материалов.
Макс, почему редкие трюфели оказались на помойке?
examples.trans: Max, why did rare truffles end up in the dumpster?

examples.text: Но вы обязаны распробовать этот редкий шедевр!
examples.trans: But you must taste this rare masterpiece!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'seriously'.
once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'frying pan', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('skillet') (shallow cooking pan) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Рыба почти готова на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: The fish is almost ready on the hot pan.

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: а вы случайно не...? = are you by any chance...?
Secondary conversational sense ('by accident, unintentionally') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Извините, а вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Hello! Excuse me, are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'равнивать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to compare', forming an aspectual pair with 'сравнить'.

examples.text: Вы серьёзно сравниваете меня с французским мастером?
examples.trans: Are you seriously comparing me with a French master?

examples.text: Возьми кусочек, чтобы сравнивать свой вкус.
examples.trans: Take a piece so that you can compare your taste.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'talent', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: У этой девочки большой талант к музыке.
examples.trans: This girl has a great talent for music.

examples.text: Потому что твой папа прав! У тебя нет таланта.
examples.trans: Because your dad is right! You have no talent.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'equipment, machinery, technique' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('technique, skill') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Step aside away from the equipment!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

учиться.gloss: to study, to be a student; to learn

meanings.en: to study, to be a student
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'читься'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to study', forming an aspectual pair with 'научиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

meanings.en: to learn how to do something
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('to learn how to do something') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Но вы же с ним учились вместе!
examples.trans: But you studied together with him!

examples.text: А я всё выучила. Я хорошо учусь.
examples.trans: And I've learned everything. I do well at school.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('French').

examples.trans: And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: in comparisons: больше, чем = more than

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
examples.trans: Why not? A sales assistant earns more than a lecturer.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
